notes:
K8Secret 0.6.13 — client certificates on macOS 26.

This is the fix for clusters that authenticate with a client certificate and failed with 'a TLS error caused the secure connection to fail' — particularly on macOS 26, while kubectl worked fine against the same cluster with the same kubeconfig.

macOS asks an app for a client certificate through a different callback than the one it uses for checking the server's certificate. Older versions of macOS, if an app only answered the second, quietly redirected the first to it as well. macOS 26 does not. K8Secret only answered the second — so the server asked for your certificate, nothing replied, none was sent, and the cluster closed the connection. The handshake itself was perfect, which is why the error blamed TLS and told you nothing.

K8Secret now answers both, so it no longer matters which one a given version of macOS uses.

With thanks to the person who ran the diagnostics on the machine where this actually happened. Three releases of careful guessing from a machine where it worked found nothing; one trace from the machine where it failed found it immediately.
